title: UNIT FIVE: POLITICS, ECONOMY, AND SOCIAL PROCESSES FROM THE EARLY SIXTEENTH TO THE END OF THE EIGHTEENTH CENTURIES
content:
ሰላም ሰላም! የተወደዳችሁና የምንወዳችሁ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን! 🌟👋❤️ እንደምን ቆያችሁልን? ዛሬ ደግሞ የHistory of Ethiopia and the Horn (Hist. 1012) የምዕራፍ አምስት Part 3 Tutorial ይዘንላችሁ ቀርበናል! በዚህ ክፍል በምዕራፍ 5 ክፍል 5.5 ስር የሚገኙትን የምሥራቅ፣ የማዕከላዊ፣ የደቡብ፣ የደቡብ-ምዕራብ እና የምዕራብ ኢትዮጵያ ሕዝቦችና መንግሥታት ታሪክ በዝርዝር እንመለከታለን።👇👇👇! ☕📚🔥

5.5. Peoples and States in Eastern, Central, Southern and Western Parts of the Region

• General Overview: It is impossible to exhaustively cover all the peoples and states in a brief teaching module. However, this section explores key representative societies. Separating them into regional categories does not mean they existed in isolation; they maintained vibrant long-distance trade, political alliances, and cultural contacts across the Horn of Africa.

5.5.1. Peoples and States in the East

• The Emirate of Harar:
- Walled City & Dynastic Foundations: During the reign of Emir Nur Mujahid, Harar became a walled city (Jugol). Later, Emir Ali ibn Da'ud (r. 1647–62) founded a new dynasty that ruled the Emirate for over two and a half centuries. The Emirate was further strengthened by subsequent rulers such as Amir Abdul Shakur (1783–94).
- Governance & Administration: The Amir's governance was assisted by a council called Majlis. The council supervised mosque-owned land known as waqf. Over time, the Amirs extended political, economic, and religious influence over surrounding Afar, Argobba, Oromo, and Somali populations through trade networks, intermarriage, and Islamic teachings.

👉
1. የሐረር ኤሚሬት (The Emirate of Harar): በኤሚር ኑር ሙጃሂድ ጊዜ ሐረር በግንብ (Jugol) ተከበበች። በ1647 ኤሚር አሊ እብን ዳዉድ አዲስ ሥረወ-መንግሥት መሠረተ።
2. የአስተዳደር ሥርዓት: ኤሚሩን የሚያማክር Majlis የተባለ ምክር ቤት የነበረ ሲሆን፣ የ መስጊድ መሬትን (waqf) ይቆጣጠር ነበር። ኤሚሬቱ ከአፋር፣ አርጎብባ፣ ኦሮሞ እና ሶማሌ ጋር በንግድ፣ በጋብቻና በሃይማኖት ተሳስሮ ነበር።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Founder of the Harar Dynasty (1647): Emir Ali ibn Da'ud.
• Council Assisting the Amir: Majlis.
• Mosque Land Property Managed by Majlis: Waqf.

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: የሐረር ኤሚሮች እኮ የWaqf መሬት አስተዳደር ላይ በጣም ጥብቅ ነበሩ፤ ያለ Majlis ፈቃድ አንዲት ሳንቲም ወይም መሬት ንቅንቅ የለም! 🏰📜


5.5.2. Peoples and States in Central and South Central Parts

• The Kingdom of Shewa:
- Foundational Lineage: Founded by Negasi Kristos (r. 1696–1703) from Gera Meder in Menz, who claimed descent from Abeto Yaqob (son of Emperor Lebne-Dengel), initiating the Shewan Solomonid branch. He unified Christian communities in Asendabo, Debadebo, and Makfud, while allying with low-land Argobba Muslims in Yifat.
- Succession of Rulers:
* Merid Azmatch Sebestie/Sebastyanos (r. 1703–18).
* Abuye/Abiyye (r. 1718–45): Made Haramba his capital; attempted to subjugate surrounding Oromos but was killed by the Karrayu Oromo.
* Amaha Iyesus/Amhayyes (r. 1745–75): Asserted control over Bulga, Efrata, Menz, and Tegulet; established capitals at Doqaqit and later Ankober.
* Asfa-Wosen (r. 1775–1808): Conquered Antsokia, Asbo, Gedem, Gishe, Merhabete, Morat, and Shewa Meda. Base economy: agriculture, trade, and craft.
• Gurage:
- Clans & Social Structure: Divided into Sebat Bet Gurage (Western Gurage: Chaha, Muher, Ezha, Gumer, Inamor, Endegegn/Enner, Gyeto) and Northern Gurage (Kistane/Aymalal/Soddo), alongside Dobbi, Gadabano, and Masqan.
- Governance & Economy: Decentralized system governed by traditional legal codes: Yajoka Qicha (Sebat Bet) and Gordanna Sera (Kistane). Military and political authority was held by titles like abegaz or azmatch. Staple crop: enset (false banana).
• Silte:
- Origins & Migration: Traced to notables like Hajji Aliye who migrated from Chercher highlands before the 16th century. Ethnogenesis formed through demographic mixing during Christian-Adal wars and Oromo movements.
- Economy: High-land staple was enset; low-lands relied on cereals. Cash crops: Khat and berbere (red pepper), along with coffee trading.
• Hadiya:
- History & Composition: Dates to the 13th century. Population expanded into subgroups: Mareko, Lemu, Soro, Shashogo, and Badowacho.
- Diplomatic Ties: Stabilized relations with the Christian state, highlighted by Emperor Zara-Yaqob marrying Hadiya princess Ite Jan Zela (Queen Elleni).
• Kambata:
- Formation & Governance: Formed between 1550–1570 by four communities (Kambata proper, Dubamo, Donga, Tembaro). Governed by a 7-member Hambericho Council representing seven dominant clans (Kambata Lamala), headed by a king. Economy: enset cultivation.
• Halaba:
- Location & Administration: Settled between Bilate River and Lake Hawassa. Led by a Woma (king) and clan leaders forming the Halabi Ogete assembly, functioning based on Sera (traditional laws).
- Economy: Agriculture, livestock, cash crops (red pepper, maize, teff); primary trade center was Kolito.

👉
1. የሸዋ መንግሥት (Kingdom of Shewa): በነጋሲ ክርስቶስ የተመሠረተ ሲሆን፣ አብይ መዲናውን ሐራምባ አድርጎ በከራዩ ኦሮሞዎች ተገደለ። አማሐ ኢየሱስ መዲናውን ወደ አንኮበር አዛወረ።
2. ጉራጌ (Gurage): በስባት ቤት እና በኪስታኔ የተከፈሉ ናቸው። ባህላዊ ሕጎቻቸው Yajoka Qicha (ለስባት ቤት) እና Gordanna Sera (ለኪስታኔ) ይባላሉ። ዋና ምግባቸው እንሰት ነው።
3. ስልጤ (Silte): መነሻቸው ከሀጂ አሊዬ የመጣ ሲሆን፣ ጫትና በርበሬ ዋና የንግድ ሰብሎቻቸው ነበሩ።
4. ሃዲያ (Hadiya): ከ13ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን ጀምሮ የነበረ ሲሆን፣ ንግሥት እሌኒ (እቴ ጃን ዜላ) የሃዲያ ልዕልት ነበረች።
5. ከምባታና ሀላባ: ከምባታ በHambericho Council (የ7 አባላት ምክር ቤት) ይተዳደራል። ሀላባ በWoma (ንጉሥ) እና በHalabi Ogete የሽማግሌዎች ስብሰባ የሚመራ ሲሆን ዋና ማዕከሉ ኮሊቶ ነበር።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Founder of Shewan Dynasty & Capital of Amaha Iyesus: Negasi Kristos & Ankober.
• Traditional Legal Codes of Gurage: Yajoka Qicha & Gordanna Sera.
• Hadiya Princess Married to Emperor Zara-Yaqob: Queen Elleni (Ite Jan Zela).
• Governing Assembly of Kambata & Halaba: Hambericho Council & Halabi Ogete.

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: አጼ ዛራ ያዕቆብ እኮ ንግሥት እሌኒን ሲያገባ የፖለቲካ ዲፕሎማሲውንም የክትፎ ፍቅርንም አጣምሮ ይዞ ነው! 👑🥘


5.5.3. Peoples and States in the South

• Sidama:
- Governance & Social Order: Political authority held by the Mote (king) in consultation with the Songo (council of elders). Spiritual affairs (sacrifices, circumcision, marriage) were handled by the Woma.
- Age-Grade System: Social order structured into 8-year generation sets called Luwa (5 grades: Darara, Fullassa, Hirbora, Wawassa, Mogissa). Justice was guided by the moral code of Halale (ultimate truth). Main crops: enset and coffee.
• Gedeo:
- Lineage & Administration: Ancestry traced to Daraso (older brother of Gujo, father of Guji Oromo). Seven clans divided into two houses: Shole Batte (senior house - 4 clans) and Sase Batte (junior house - 3 clans).
- Balle System: Traditional governance called balle based on 7 age-classes across a 70-year cycle (10 years per grade). Territory governed under a federation called Sasserogo sharing one Abba Gadaa rotated every 8 years. Economy: enset cultivation.
• Konso:
- Agriculture & Settlement: Famous for specialized agricultural techniques, specifically stone terracing to control soil erosion on rugged hills. Inhabited fortified walled villages called paletas, divided into wards called kanta.
- Governance: Administered by a council of elders called hayyota, selected with adult male participation, rotating every 18 years.

👉
1. ሲዳማ (Sidama): በMote (ንጉሥ) እና በSongo (የሽማግሌዎች ምክር ቤት) ይመራል። የ8 ዓመት እድሜ እርከን Luwa ሲባል፣ የፍትሕና ሞራል መመሪያቸው Halale (እውነት) ይባላል።
2. ጌዴኦ (Gedeo): በShole Batte እና Sase Batte የተከፈሉ 7 ጎሣዎች አሏቸው። የBalle ሥርዓት በየ10 ዓመቱ የሚቀያየር 7 ደረጃዎች አሉት። ግዛታቸው Sasserogo ይባላል።
3. ኮንሶ (Konso): በድንጋይ እርከን (Terraces) እና በታጠሩ መንደሮች (paletas) ይታወቃሉ። አስተዳደራቸው በhayyota (የሽማግሌዎች ምክር ቤት) በየ18 ዓመቱ ይተካል።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Moral Code & Generation Sets of Sidama: Halale & Luwa.
• Governance System & Federation of Gedeo: Balle & Sasserogo.
• Konso Walled Villages & Council of Elders: Paletas & Hayyota.

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: የኮንሶ ሰዎች እርከን ከመሥራታቸው የተነሣ ኮረብታ ያገኙበት ቦታ ላይ ሁሉ እርሻ መሥራት ይወዳሉ፤ መሬት ቁልቁለት ከሆነ ለእነሱ አዲስ Farms ቻሌንጅ ነው!💪⛰️🌾


5.5.4. Peoples and States in the Southwest

• Wolayta:
- Dynasties & Power Structure: Ruled successively by the Wolayta-Malla and Tigre dynasties. Reached peak power in the late 18th/early 19th centuries. Led by the Kawo (king) supported by an advisors' council. Land was granted by the Kawo based on military valor; staple crop was enset.
• Yem:
- Political Structure & Defense: Initially ruled by Dida/Halmam-Gamma dynasty until ousted in the 14th century, followed by the Mowa (Howa) dynasty. Headed by Amno (king/chief priest with divine attributes) assisted by 12 advisors called astessor. Provincial/district governors were erasho and gagna. Dug protective ditches (bero) and erected 50-meter pillars at Brisi Bita for military patrols.
• Dawuro:
- Formation & Defense: Composed of Malla, Dogolla, and Amara clans. The Kawuka dynasty created a unified state under famous kings like Kati Irashu and Kati Halala around 1700. Renowned for extensive defensive stone walls.
• Gamo:
- Village Autonomy: Inhabited areas around Lakes Chamo and Abaya to Gughe Mountain. Governed by customary law called woga. Organized into autonomous villages called dere, featuring kawo (hereditary ritual leader), halaqa (initiates), and dubusha (assembly site) where the dulata assembly elected leaders called huduga/maga.
• Ari:
- Clans & Authority: Organized into 10 independent clans led by a hereditary chief called babi, assisted by godimis (religious leaders), zis (village heads), and tsoikis (intelligence agents).
• Kafa:
- State Organization & Defense: Emerged in the 14th century, expanding under the Minjo dynasty. The king, Tato, was advised by a 7-member council called Mikrecho. Capital was Andaracha. Traded ivory, gold, slaves, coffee, and civet musk. Dug deep protective trenches called erio.

👉
1. ወላይታ (Wolayta): በWolayta-Malla እና Tigre ሥረወ-መንግሥታት የተመራ፤ ንጉሡ Kawo ይባላል።
2. የም (Yem): በMowa ሥረወ-መንግሥት የተመራ፤ ንጉሡ Amno ሲሆን 12 astessor የተባሉ አማካሪዎች ነበሩት። ለደኅንነት bero (ካናሎች) እና በBrisi Bita 50 ሜትር የብረት/እንጨት ቋሚዎችን ተክለዋል።
3. ዳውሮ (Dawuro): በKawuka ሥረወ-መንግሥት (በKati Halala) የተገነባ፤ በድንጋይ የተሠሩ የቆጠራ መከላከያ ግንቦች አሏቸው።
4. ጋሞ (Gamo): በdere በተባሉ መንደሮች ተደራጅተው በwoga ሕግ ይተዳደራሉ፤ የመሰብሰቢያ ቦታቸው dubusha ይባላል።
5. አሪ (Ari): በ10 ጎሣዎች የተከፈሉ ሲሆን መሪያቸው babi ይባላል፤ tsoikis የተባሉ የደኅንነት መረጃ ሰበሰቢዎች ነበሯቸው።
6. ከፋ (Kafa): በMinjo ሥረወ-መንግሥት የተመራ፤ ንጉሡ Tato በ7ቱ Mikrecho አማካሪዎች ይረዳል። የመከላከያ ጉድጓዶቻቸው erio ይባላሉ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Title of Wolayta & Kafa Kings: Kawo (Wolayta) & Tato (Kafa).
• Yem Protective Trenches & 12 Advisors: Bero & Astessor.
• Dawuro Wall Builder King: Kati Halala.
• Gamo Assembly Site & Ari Intelligence Agents: Dubusha & Tsoikis.
• Kafa Advisory Council & Protective Trenches: Mikrecho & Erio.




5.5.5. Peoples and States in the West

• Anywa:
- Settlement & Governance: Settled along the Pibor, Sobat, Gila, Akobo, Agwei, Oboth, Baro, and Alwero Rivers in Gambella. Southern Anywa trace origins to founder Oshoda. Governed by village chiefs called kuaari, assisted by nobles called nyiye to allocate land and settle disputes.
• Majang:
- Migration & Livelihood: Origin traced to Boma plateau in South Sudan, extending towards Dembi-Dollo. Practiced shifting cultivation, animal husbandry, beekeeping, hunting, and fishing.
• Nuer:
- Social Structure: Inhabited plains of Gambella along Sobat and Baro Rivers and Bahr el-Ghazal (Sudan). Maintained an age-set system combining social and political functions. Boys passed rigorous tests and initiation rites to transition into adulthood.
• Berta and Gumuz:
- Location & Trade: Lived along the lower course of the Abbay River. Had long-standing trade with northern Sudan, leading to strong Islamic influence. Rich gold deposits attracted external traders.
• Kunama:
- Customs & Economy: Also known as Baza, living along Gash, Tekkeze, and Tigray regions. Customary institution called sanga-anene handled administration, asylum, and murder reconciliation rituals. Office inherited matrilineally from eldest brother to nephew. Economy based on hoe/plough agriculture (staple: kina/sorghum) and livestock.

👉
1. አኙዋክ (Anywa): በጋምቤላ አበቦች አካባቢ የሚኖሩ ሲሆን፣ በkuaari (መንደር አለቃ) እና በnyiye (መኳንንት) ይተዳደራሉ።
2. ማጃንግ (Majang): ከመቀያየር እርሻ (Shifting cultivation)፣ ከንብ ማር እና ከአደን ጋር የተያያዘ ኑሮ ነበራቸው።
3. ኑዌር (Nuer): ለአዋቂነት የሚያበቃ ጥብቅ የፈተና እና የእድሜ እርከን (Age-set) ሥርዓት አላቸው።
4. በርታ እና ጉሙዝ: በአባይ ወንዝ በታችኛው ክፍል የሚኖሩ ሲሆን፣ በንግድ ምክንያት የእስልምና ተፅዕኖ የነበረባቸውና በወርቅ ሀብታቸው የሚታወቁ ነበሩ።
5. ኩናማ (Kunama): Baza በመባልም ይታወቃሉ። Sanga-anene የተባለ በዕናት መስመር (Matrilineal) የሚተላለፍ የእርቅና የአስተዳደር ተቋም አላቸው። ዋና እህላቸው kina (ማሽላ) ነው።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Anywa Village Chief & Nobles: Kuaari & Nyiye.
• Kunama Customary Institution & Inheritance Lineage: Sanga-anene & Matrilineal.
• Kunama Staple Crop: Kina (Sorghum).
